TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: abbrev LPNChal (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) : Type
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: The LPN challenge is exactly the canonical challenge of the construction's LWE-family view [JLS26, Lemma 4.2, p. 19]. Dv3 uses the family's independent dimension L and matrix orientation.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: theorem lpnChal_eq (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) : P.LPNChal π L = (Matrix (Fin ((P.lpnFamily_raw π).toLWE.parameters L).samples) (Fin ((P.lpnFamily_raw π).toLWE.parameters L).dimension) (ZMod ((P.lpnFamily_raw π).toLWE.parameters L).modulus) × (Fin ((P.lpnFamily_raw π).toLWE.parameters L).samples → ZMod ((P.lpnFamily_raw π).toLWE.parameters L).modulus))
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: The canonical challenge is its displayed LWE matrix/value product. Glue reader.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: noncomputable def lpnEnc (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) (x : P.LPNChal π L) : List Bool
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: LPN encoding is exactly the assumption's `LWE.encodeChallenge`, with its own residue width [JLS26, Lemma 4.2, p. 19]. Dv3 changes no assumption challenge or encoding.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: theorem lpnEnc_eq (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) (x : P.LPNChal π L) : P.lpnEnc π L x = LWE.encodeChallenge ((P.lpnFamily_raw π).toLWE.parameters L) ((P.lpnFamily_raw π).toLWE.residueBits.eval L) x
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: The LPN encoding is the unchanged canonical family challenge code. Glue reader.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: theorem lpn_dimension_eq (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) : ((P.lpnFamily_raw π).toLWE.parameters L).dimension = L
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: Canonical LPN secret dimension equals L. Glue composed from owner-side parameter readers.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: theorem lpn_samples_eq (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) : ((P.lpnFamily_raw π).toLWE.parameters L).samples = L ^ P.D
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: Canonical LPN sample count equals L^D. Glue composed from owner-side parameter readers.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: theorem lpn_modulus_eq (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) : ((P.lpnFamily_raw π).toLWE.parameters L).modulus = (π (P.kappaOf L)).p
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: Canonical LPN modulus is the prime at inverse dimension. Glue composed from owner readers.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: abbrev LPNConcrete (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) : Type
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: Concrete LPN coordinates expose rows L^D, columns L and the inverse-indexed prime [JLS26, Lemma 4.2, p. 19]. Dv3 and Dv15 use only explicit transport from the assumption.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: theorem lpnConcrete_eq (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) : P.LPNConcrete π L = (Matrix (Fin (L ^ P.D)) (Fin L) (ZMod (π (P.kappaOf L)).p) × (Fin (L ^ P.D) → ZMod (π (P.kappaOf L)).p))
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: Concrete LPN coordinates have the displayed finite matrix/value type. Glue reader.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: noncomputable def lpnChalEquiv (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) : P.LPNChal π L ≃ P.LPNConcrete π L
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: Canonical and concrete LPN challenges are related by explicit finite and residue casts [JLS26, Lemma 4.2, p. 19]. Dv15 uses `finCongr` and `Equiv.cast`, with no chosen enumeration.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: theorem lpnChalEquiv_eq (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) : P.lpnChalEquiv π L = Equiv.prodCongr (Equiv.arrowCongr (finCongr (P.lpn_samples_eq π L)) (Equiv.arrowCongr (finCongr (P.lpn_dimension_eq π L)) (Equiv.cast (congrArg ZMod (P.lpn_modulus_eq π L))))) (Equiv.arrowCongr (finCongr (P.lpn_samples_eq π L)) (Equiv.cast (congrArg ZMod (P.lpn_modulus_eq π L))))
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: The challenge equivalence is its explicit product/arrow/finite-cast composition. Glue.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: structure LPNAdvice (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ)
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: Advice retains the hop, Boolean index, buckets, exact draw, Boolean tail and uniform vectors [JLS26, Lemma 4.2, p. 19]. Dv12 hardwires averaged values rather than sampling; the extra hop sentinel `Fin (κ+1)` keeps the type inhabited at every independent dimension L.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: abbrev LPNAdviceProduct (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) : Type
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: Advice has the explicit right-associated finite product of its six components. Glue.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: theorem lpnAdviceProduct_eq (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) : P.LPNAdviceProduct π L = (Fin (P.kappaOf L + 1) × (P.G.Idx (P.n (P.kappaOf L)) × ((Fin (P.m (P.kappaOf L)) → Fin (P.B (P.kappaOf L))) × (P.Draw (P.kappaOf L) (π (P.kappaOf L)) × ((Fin (P.m (P.kappaOf L)) → Bool) × (Fin (P.kappaOf L) → Fin (P.n (P.kappaOf L)) → ZMod (π (P.kappaOf L)).p))))))
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: The advice product is the displayed right-associated tuple. Glue reader.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: def lpnAdviceProductEquiv (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) : P.LPNAdvice π L ≃ P.LPNAdviceProduct π L
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: Advice records and their explicit component products are equivalent. Glue for Dv15.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: theorem lpnAdviceProductEquiv_apply (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) (w : P.LPNAdvice π L) : P.lpnAdviceProductEquiv π L w = (w.hop, w.I, w.buckets, w.draw, w.tail, w.uniform)
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: Advice-product transport reads precisely the record's six fields. Glue reader.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: theorem lpnAdviceProductEquiv_symm_apply (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) (w : P.LPNAdviceProduct π L) : (P.lpnAdviceProductEquiv π L).symm w = ⟨w.1, w.2.1, w.2.2.1, w.2.2.2.1, w.2.2.2.2.1, w.2.2.2.2.2⟩
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: Inverse advice-product transport constructs the record from its six coordinates. Glue reader.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: noncomputable def lpnAdviceCard (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) : ℕ
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: The explicit advice coordinate count is the product of its six finite cardinalities. Glue.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: theorem lpnAdviceCard_eq (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) : P.lpnAdviceCard π L = let κ
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: The advice coordinate count is the stated nested product. Glue reader.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: noncomputable def lpnAdviceEquiv (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) : P.LPNAdvice π L ≃ Fin (P.lpnAdviceCard π L)
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: Advice has explicit Fin coordinates assembled from its supplied and canonical equivalences [JLS26, Lemma 4.2, p. 19]. Dv15 uses no classical finite enumeration.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: theorem lpnAdviceEquiv_eq (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) : P.lpnAdviceEquiv π L = let κ
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: Advice Fin coordinates use the displayed tail/draw/bucket/index product composition. Glue.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: noncomputable instance instLPNAdviceFintype (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) : Fintype (P.LPNAdvice π L)
theorem instLPNAdviceFintype_eq (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) : instLPNAdviceFintype P π L = Fintype.ofEquiv (Fin (P.lpnAdviceCard π L)) (P.lpnAdviceEquiv π L).symm
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: The LPN advice finiteness instance is induced by its explicit Fin equivalence; glue.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: instance instLPNAdviceNonempty (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) : Nonempty (P.LPNAdvice π L)
noncomputable def encLPNAdvice (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) (w : P.LPNAdvice π L) : List Bool
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: Advice encoding begins with the prime and unary L, followed by its six explicit components [JLS26, Lemma 4.2, p. 19]. Dv9, Dv12 and Dv15 give the preprocessor all parameters as input; the hardwired tail avoids calling the PRG. No sampler or choice-based code occurs here.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: theorem encLPNAdvice_eq (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) (w : P.LPNAdvice π L) : P.encLPNAdvice π L w = let κ
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: Advice encoding is the displayed prime-first nested pair of all six fields. Glue reader.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: def lpnAdviceBound (P : Params) : PolyExpr
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: A syntactic bound for all encoded LPN advice is `4096*(L+1)*S(L)^3`, where S sums index, seed, output, Boolean-seed and secret bounds and L+1. Glue for Dv12 and Dv15. The generous constant bounds all nested separators without an asymptotic hidden factor.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: theorem lpnAdviceBound_eq (P : Params) : P.lpnAdviceBound = .mul (.const 4096) (.mul (.add .var (.const 1)) (.pow (.add P.idxBound (.add P.seedBound (.add P.mBound (.add P.nBound (.add P.ellBound (.add .var (.const 1))))))) 3))
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: The LPN advice bound is its displayed syntactic polynomial. Glue reader.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: noncomputable def lpnMatrixAt (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) (h : L = P.ℓ (P.kappaOf L)) (x : P.LPNChal π L) : Matrix (Fin (P.n (P.kappaOf L))) (Fin (P.ℓ (P.kappaOf L))) (ZMod (π (P.kappaOf L)).p)
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: On a scheduled dimension, the challenged matrix is transported to the exact κ dimensions [JLS26, Lemma 4.2, p. 19]. Dv15 uses only `finCongr` and published length equations.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: theorem lpnMatrixAt_eq (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) (h : L = P.ℓ (P.kappaOf L)) (x : P.LPNChal π L) : P.lpnMatrixAt π L h x = fun i a => (P.lpnChalEquiv π L x).1 ((finCongr ((congrArg (fun q : ℕ => q ^ P.D) h).trans (P.n_eq (P.kappaOf L)).symm)).symm i) ((finCongr h).symm a)
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: The matrix transport is the displayed explicit row/column finite cast. Glue reader.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: noncomputable def lpnValuesAt (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) (h : L = P.ℓ (P.kappaOf L)) (x : P.LPNChal π L) : Fin (P.n (P.kappaOf L)) → ZMod (π (P.kappaOf L)).p
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: On a scheduled dimension, challenged values use the corresponding explicit row transport [JLS26, Lemma 4.2, p. 19]. Dv15 changes no challenge coordinate.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: theorem lpnValuesAt_eq (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) (h : L = P.ℓ (P.kappaOf L)) (x : P.LPNChal π L) : P.lpnValuesAt π L h x = fun i => (P.lpnChalEquiv π L x).2 ((finCongr ((congrArg (fun q : ℕ => q ^ P.D) h).trans (P.n_eq (P.kappaOf L)).symm)).symm i)
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: Value transport is the displayed row cast of the concrete challenge. Glue reader.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: noncomputable def lpnPre (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) (w : P.LPNAdvice π L) (x : P.LPNChal π L) : List Bool
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: LPN preprocessing replaces the chosen instance by challenged values plus σ, leaves earlier instances uniform and later instances real, and publishes the hardwired tail with error zero [JLS26, Lemma 4.2, p. 19]. Dv12 uses only advice and the challenge; it neither samples nor calls PRG evaluation. Off the schedule image it returns the empty word.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: theorem lpnPre_eq (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) (w : P.LPNAdvice π L) (x : P.LPNChal π L) : P.lpnPre π L w x = let κ
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: LPN preprocessing is its guarded, deterministic hybrid challenge construction. Glue reader.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: noncomputable def lpnRed (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (A : NUPPT) (L : ℕ) (w : P.LPNAdvice π L) (x : P.LPNChal π L) (r : List Bool) : List Bool
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: The explicit LPN reduction invokes A at κOf(L) with preprocessing and a coin prefix [JLS26, Lemma 4.2, p. 19]. Dv12 and Dv14 separate its typed function from its machine; advice is an input and no machine or sampler is constructed.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: theorem lpnRed_eq (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (A : NUPPT) (L : ℕ) (w : P.LPNAdvice π L) (x : P.LPNChal π L) (r : List Bool) : P.lpnRed π A L w x r = A.runAtL (P.kappaOf L) (P.lpnPre π L w x) (r.take (A.coinLen (P.kappaOf L)))
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: The reduction calls A on its preprocessed challenge and the stated prefix. Glue reader.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: def LPNRealizable (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) : Prop
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: LPN realizability says every adversary and every polynomially bounded typed advice family has a machine realizing the explicit reduction. [JLS26, Lemma 4.2, p. 19]. Dv14 leaves this as the named Phase B obligation; the target link supplies it without constructing machines here. Dv16 uses shared RealizesOn on encoded challenges and layout-length coins only, which admits more realisers and makes this proposition easier than its every-string draft.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: theorem LPNRealizable_iff (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) : P.LPNRealizable π ↔ ∀ (A : NUPPT) (w : ∀ L, P.LPNAdvice π L), ∃ B : NUPPT, B.RealizesOn (P.lpnEnc π) (A.coins.subst .var) (fun L x r => P.lpnRed π A L (w L) x r)
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: LPN realizability is the explicit contract for every adversary and advice family. Glue reader.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: theorem lpnEnc_injective (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) : Function.Injective (P.lpnEnc π L)
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: Canonical LPN challenge encoding is injective [JLS26, Lemma 4.2, p. 19]. Dv3 reuses the assumption's width and canonical encoder unchanged.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: theorem encLPNAdvice_injective (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) : Function.Injective (P.encLPNAdvice π L)
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: All six hardwired advice fields are retained by the explicit code [JLS26, Lemma 4.2, p. 19]. Dv9 and Dv15 place the prime first and use fixed coordinate codes.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: theorem encLPNAdvice_length_le (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (L : ℕ) (w : P.LPNAdvice π L) : (P.encLPNAdvice π L w).length ≤ P.lpnAdviceBound.eval L
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: Every advice word has length at most the explicit polynomial at its independent dimension [JLS26, Lemma 4.2, p. 19]. Dv12 and Dv15 count hardwired data rather than sampler coins.

TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.header: theorem lpn_hop (P : Params) (π : PrimeSchedule) (A : NUPPT) (tails : ℕ → Bool) (hops : ∀ κ, Fin (κ + 1)) : ∃ w : ∀ L, P.LPNAdvice π L, ∀ B : NUPPT, B.RealizesOn (P.lpnEnc π) (A.coins.subst .var) (fun L x r => P.lpnRed π A L (w L) x r) → ∀ κ, (hops κ).val < κ → Games.advantage (P.chainGame A (tails κ) (hops κ).val κ (π κ)) (P.chainGame A (tails κ) ((hops κ).val + 1) κ (π κ)) ≤ (P.lpnFamily_raw π).adv B (P.ℓ κ)
TCSlib.Cryptography.Obfuscation.Structur.statement_prose: One advice family bounds any selected LPN hop for every realizing non-uniform PPT machine [JLS26, Lemma 4.2, p. 19]. Dv8 and Dv12 retain buckets and hardwire averaged values. Dv16 uses the shared, layout-length-only RealizesOn; more realisers are admitted, so this security statement is at least as strong as the every-coin-string draft. The sentinel hop makes advice inhabited at κ=0; the hop inequality is requested only below κ.
